-- a local that a closure assigns, read as an argument before a call that runs the closure
local n = 1
local function bump()
	n += 10
	return n
end

local max = math.max
local obj = {}
function obj:show(...)
	return select("#", ...), ...
end

print(n, bump(), n)
print(math.max(n, bump()), n)
print(max(n, bump()), n)
print(obj:show(n, bump(), n))
print(tostring(n) .. tostring(bump()), n)
local t = { n, bump(), n }
print(t[1], t[2], t[3])
print(n + bump(), n)
print(select(2, n, bump(), n))

-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls

local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))
flush("compare")
print(not (note("l", 1) <= note("r", 2)), note("l", 2) ~= note("r", 2))
flush("compare not")
if note("cond l", 5) > note("cond r", 4) then
	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

-- the object of a method call is worked out once, before its arguments
local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

-- a value read into a local before the table changes keeps the old value
local t = { v = "old" }
local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)
local box = { 1, 2, 3 }
local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

-- a call that changes a local the same argument list reads before and after it
local counter = 0
local function bump()
	counter += 1
	return counter
end
print(counter, bump(), counter + 0, bump())
local before = counter
bump()
print(before, counter)

-- an index read before a call in the same expression moves it

local i = 1
local function advance()
	i += 1
	return 0
end
print(arr[i] + advance(), arr[i])

-- every operand runs left to right before anything combines, right-associative or not

flush("concat")
print(note("x", 2) ^ note("y", 3) ^ note("z", 1), note("p", 10) - note("q", 3) - note("r", 2))
flush("arith")

-- and / or only run what they need

print(hit)
flush("logic")

flush("constructor")

-- the table writes into the old one

local function swap()
	note("swap", nil)
	local old = holder.inner
	holder.inner = { v = 100 }
	return old.v + 1
end
holder.inner.v = swap()
print(holder.inner.v)
flush("target")

-- Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding
-- lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to
-- stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.
do
	const t = {1, 2, 3}
	while local v = table.remove(t) do
		print(v, #t)
	end
end
do
	local items = {"a", "b", false, "c"}
	local i = 0
	local function nextItem()
		i += 1
		return items[i]
	end
	-- false ends the loop just like nil
	while const item = nextItem() do
		print("item", item)
	end
	print("stopped at", i)
end
do
	local fns = {}
	local queue = {10, 20, 30}
	while local n = table.remove(queue, 1) do
		table.insert(fns, function()
			return n
		end)
	end
	print(fns[1](), fns[2](), fns[3]())
end
do
	local x = "outer"
	if local x = nil then
		print("then", x)
	else
		print("else", x)
	end
	if local x = "inner" then
		print("then", x)
	end
	print("after", x)
end
do
	local function classify(s)
		if local n: number? = tonumber(s) then
			return "number " .. n * 2
		elseif local first = string.match(s, "^%a+") then
			return "word " .. first
		elseif const sym = string.match(s, "^%p") then
			return "symbol " .. sym
		else
			return "other"
		end
	end
	print(classify("21"), classify("hello world"), classify("!?"), classify("  "))
end
do
	local function lookup(t, k)
		return if local v = t[k] then v .. "!" else "missing"
	end
	local map = {a = "x", b = "y"}
	print(lookup(map, "a"), lookup(map, "z"))
	const limit = 3
	local count = 0
	while local v = count < limit and count do
		count = v + 1
	end
	print("count", count)
end

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v
end
for i = bound(1), bound(3), bound(1) do
	print("bounded", i)
end
print("bound calls", calls)

-- writing the loop variable changes only this iteration's copy
for i = 1, 3 do
	local before = i
	i = i * 10
	print("copy", before, i)
end

-- a while loop with two exits and a repeat that runs once
local n, steps = 27, 0
while true do
	if n == 1 then
		break
	end
	if steps > 200 then
		print("too long")
		break
	end
	n = if n % 2 == 0 then n // 2 else 3 * n + 1
	steps += 1
end
print("collatz", steps)
repeat
	steps -= 1
until true
print("after repeat", steps)

-- nested loops where the inner break and continue only touch the inner loop
local found = {}
for i = 1, 4 do
	for j = 1, 4 do
		if j > i then
			break
		end
		if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
			continue
		end
		found[#found + 1] = i * 10 + j
	end
end
print(table.concat(found, " "))

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v
end
for i = bound(1), bound(3), bound(1) do
	print("bounded", i)
end
print("bound calls", calls)

-- writing the loop variable changes only this iteration's copy
for i = 1, 3 do
	local before = i
	i = i * 10
	print("copy", before, i)
end

-- a while loop with two exits and a repeat that runs once
local n, steps = 27, 0
while true do
	if n == 1 then
		break
	end
	if steps > 200 then
		print("too long")
		break
	end
	n = if n % 2 == 0 then n // 2 else 3 * n + 1
	steps += 1
end
print("collatz", steps)
repeat
	steps -= 1
until true
print("after repeat", steps)

-- nested loops where the inner break and continue only touch the inner loop

for i = 1, 4 do
	for j = 1, 4 do
		if j > i then
			break
		end
		if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
			continue
		end
		found[#found + 1] = i * 10 + j
	end
end
print(table.concat(found, " "))

-- metamethods: arithmetic, comparison, concat, call, index and newindex functions, len and unm,
-- and the raw functions that skip them
local Vec = {}
Vec.__index = Vec
local function vec(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ x = x, y = y }, Vec)
end
Vec.__add = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y)
end
Vec.__sub = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y)
end
Vec.__mul = function(a, b)
	if type(a) == "number" then
		return vec(a * b.x, a * b.y)
	end
	return vec(a.x * b, a.y * b)
end
Vec.__unm = function(a)
	return vec(-a.x, -a.y)
end
Vec.__eq = function(a, b)
	return a.x == b.x and a.y == b.y
end
Vec.__lt = function(a, b)
	return a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y < b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y
end
Vec.__le = function(a, b)
	return not (b < a)
end
Vec.__len = function(a)
	return math.sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y)
end
Vec.__concat = function(a, b)
	local function s(v)
		return if type(v) == "table" then `({v.x}, {v.y})` else tostring(v)
	end
	return s(a) .. s(b)
end
Vec.__call = function(self, k)
	return self[k]
end
function Vec:dot(o)
	return self.x * o.x + self.y * o.y
end

local a, b = vec(1, 2), vec(3, 4)
local c = a + b
print(c.x, c.y, (a - b).x, (2 * a).y, (a * 3).x, (-a).x)
print(a == vec(1, 2), a ~= b, a < b, a <= b, a > b, b >= a, rawequal(a, vec(1, 2)))
print(#b, a .. b, a .. "!", "v=" .. a, a("y"), a:dot(b), Vec.dot(a, b))

-- __index and __newindex as functions, logging every access
local log = {}
local store = {}
local proxy = setmetatable({}, {
	__index = function(_, k)
		log[#log + 1] = "get " .. tostring(k)
		return store[k]
	end,
	__newindex = function(_, k, v)
		log[#log + 1] = "set " .. tostring(k)
		store[k] = v
	end,
})
proxy.a = 1
proxy.a += 1
proxy[1] = proxy.a * 10
print(proxy.a, proxy[1], rawget(proxy, "a"), table.concat(log, ","))
rawset(proxy, "raw", true)
print(proxy.raw, #log)

-- inheritance through __index chains
local Base = {}
Base.__index = Base
function Base.new(name)
	return setmetatable({ name = name }, Base)
end
function Base:hello()
	return "base " .. self.name
end
local Derived = setmetatable({}, { __index = Base })
Derived.__index = Derived
function Derived.new(name)
	local self = Base.new(name)
	return setmetatable(self, Derived)
end
function Derived:hello()
	return "derived " .. Base.hello(self)
end
local d = Derived.new("d")
print(d:hello(), getmetatable(d) == Derived, Base.hello(d))

-- comparisons a decompiler can't flip: with NaN, `not (a < b)` isn't `a >= b`, and `x ~= x` is
-- true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins
local nan = 0 / 0
local values = { 1, -1, 0, nan, math.huge, -math.huge }

local function compare(a, b)
	local out = {}
	if not (a < b) then out[#out + 1] = "!lt" end
	if not (a <= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!le" end
	if not (a > b) then out[#out + 1] = "!gt" end
	if not (a >= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!ge" end
	if a ~= a then out[#out + 1] = "self" end
	if not (a == b) then out[#out + 1] = "!eq" end
	while not (a < b) do
		out[#out + 1] = "w"
		break
	end
	local rounds = 0
	repeat
		rounds += 1
		out[#out + 1] = "r"
	until not (a > b) or rounds == 2
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

for i = 1, #values do
	for j = 1, #values do
		print(i, j, compare(values[i], values[j]))
	end
end

-- values, not just truthiness
local function pick(a, b, c)
	local x = a and b or c
	local y = a and (b or c)
	local z = (a or b) and c
	local w = not a == not b
	local v = a and false or c
	local u = a == nil and b or nil
	return x, y, z, w, v, u
end
local samples = { true, false, nil, 0, "", nan }
for i = 1, 6 do
	for j = 1, 6 do
		for k = 1, 6 do
			local a, b, c = samples[i], samples[j], samples[k]
			print(i, j, k, pick(a, b, c))
		end
	end
end

-- a guard whose branches both fall through, around a comparison with a constant on the left
local count = 0
for _, v in ipairs(values) do
	if 0 < v then
		count += 1
	elseif not (0 >= v) then
		count += 100
	end
end
print("count", count)

-- shapes from inlined helpers with control flow (-O2 copies them into their callers)

local flags = { force = false, edge = true }
local layers = { get = function(_, key) return { fromEdge = key == "edge" } end }
local urls = {}
urls.delivery = "https://delivery/"
urls.plain = "https://plain/"

-- early returns, one inside a condition with a call in it, inlined into an argument
local function resolveHost()
	if flags.force then
		return urls.delivery
	end
	if flags.edge then
		local data = layers:get("edge")
		if data and data.fromEdge then
			return urls.delivery
		end
	end
	return urls.plain
end
local function fetchIcons(ids)
	return string.format("%sicons?ids=%s", resolveHost(), table.concat(ids, ","))
end
print(fetchIcons({ 1, 2 }))
flags.edge = false
print(fetchIcons({ 3 }))

-- a return from inside a loop
local function hasName(names, name)
	if type(names) == "table" then
		for _, n in names do
			if n == name then
				return true
			end
		end
	elseif type(names) == "string" then
		return names == name
	end
	return false
end
local function matches(schema, value)
	if schema.kind ~= value.kind or schema.name ~= nil and not hasName(schema.name, value.name) then
		return "no"
	end
	return "yes"
end
print(matches({ kind = 1, name = { "a", "b" } }, { kind = 1, name = "b" }), matches({ kind = 1, name = "x" }, { kind = 1, name = "y" }))

-- `return a and b and f()`, with f returning early
local vr = false
local function supported()
	if vr then
		return flags.force
	end
	return true
end
local function enabled(a, b)
	return a and b and supported()
end
print(enabled(true, true), enabled(true, false))
vr = true
print(enabled(true, true))

-- a helper inlined into one that is inlined in turn, returning from a loop
local function escape(s)
	if s == "" then
		return "%00"
	end
	return (s:gsub("%.", "%%2E"))
end
local function segmentFor(node, known)
	if node.parent ~= nil then
		for _, entry in known do
			if entry.node == node then
				return entry.segment
			end
		end
	end
	return escape(node.name)
end
local function pathOf(node, known)
	local parts = {}
	while node do
		table.insert(parts, 1, segmentFor(node, known))
		node = node.parent
	end
	return table.concat(parts, "/")
end
local root = { name = "" }
local mid = { name = "a.b", parent = root }
local leaf = { name = "c", parent = mid }
print(pathOf(leaf, { { node = mid, segment = "M" } }), pathOf(leaf, {}))

-- a helper whose returns all lead to its caller's end
local picks, misses = {}, 0
local function pick(x)
	local hit = if x > 2 then x * 10 else nil
	if hit ~= nil then
		table.insert(picks, hit)
		return
	end
	if x < 0 then
		misses += 1
	end
end
local function onInput(kind, x, blocked)
	if kind == "click" then
		if not blocked then
			pick(x)
		end
	elseif kind == "touch" then
		misses += 100
	end
end
onInput("click", 5, false)
onInput("click", -1, false)
onInput("click", 9, true)
onInput("touch", 0, false)
print(table.concat(picks, ","), misses)

-- `continue` in a `repeat` goes to its condition
local function walk(list)
	local out, i, stack = {}, 0, list
	repeat
		i += 1
		local v = stack[i]
		if v == nil or v == false then
			continue
		end
		table.insert(out, v)
	until i >= #stack
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

-- shapes the new core used to refuse, mostly what -O2 inlining leaves behind

-- a local declared first, then a function that calls itself through it
local count = 0
local tick
tick = function(n)
	count += 1
	if n > 0 then
		tick(n - 1)
	end
end
tick(3)

-- a helper with a loop, inlined into a condition
local function isInside(node, kind)
	while node ~= nil do
		if node.kind == kind then
			return true
		end
		node = node.parent
	end
	return false
end
local tree = { kind = "leaf", parent = { kind = "quote", parent = { kind = "doc" } } }
local function check(start, kind)
	local found = start ~= nil
	if found and isInside(start, kind) then
		return "inside " .. kind
	end
	return "outside " .. kind
end

-- a helper with early returns and a local the next tests compare against
local A = { Asset = 1, Bundle = 2, Look = 3 }
local B = { GamePass = 4, Product = 5 }
local function isSupported(payload, requestType)
	if type(payload) == "table" then
		local kind = payload.kind
		if kind == A.Asset or kind == A.Bundle or kind == A.Look then
			return true
		end
	end
	if requestType == B.GamePass or requestType == B.Product then

--!rosetta-options +t1
-- type syntax, which compiles to nothing, compiled with type information on (+t1): every
-- function carries its parameter types in the bytecode, which a decompiler has to read past,
-- and casts, generics, packs and attributes all have to come back as valid Luau
type Vec = { x: number, y: number }
export type Shape = { kind: "circle", r: number } | { kind: "rect", w: number, h: number }
type Callback<T> = (T, ...any) -> boolean
type Pair<K, V> = { key: K, value: V }

local function add(a: Vec, b: Vec): Vec
	return { x = a.x + b.x, y = a.y + b.y }
end

local function area(s: Shape): number
	if s.kind == "circle" then
		return math.floor(3 * s.r * s.r)
	end
	return (s :: any).w * (s :: any).h
end

local function first<T>(list: { T }, pred: Callback<T>): T?
	for _, v in list do
		if pred(v) then
			return v
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function count(...: number): (number, number)
	local total = 0
	for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
		total += (select(i, ...))
	end
	return select("#", ...), total
end

local v = add({ x = 1, y = 2 }, { x = 3, y = 4 })
print(v.x, v.y)

	for _, v in list do

-- vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come
-- back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have
-- that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls
local function show(v)
	return string.format("%g,%g,%g", v.x, v.y, v.z)
end

local up = vector.create(0, 1, 0)
local unit = vector.create(1, 1, 1)
print(show(up), show(unit), typeof(up), up == vector.create(0, 1, 0))
print(show(vector.create(-0, 0.5, 1e300)), show(vector.create(1 / 3, 2 ^ 20, -7)))

-- arithmetic with vectors and numbers, and unary minus
local a, b = vector.create(1, 2, 3), vector.create(4, 5, 6)
print(show(a + b), show(a - b), show(a * b), show(b / a), show(a * 2), show(3 / b), show(-a), show(b // a))

-- components, and arguments known only at run time
local n = #"abcd"
local v = vector.create(n, n * 2, n // 3)
print(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)

-- the vector library
print(vector.magnitude(vector.create(3, 4, 0)), show(vector.normalize(vector.create(0, 0, 9))))
print(vector.dot(a, b), show(vector.cross(a, b)), show(vector.floor(vector.create(1.5, -1.5, 2))))
print(show(vector.ceil(vector.create(1.2, -1.2, 0))), show(vector.abs(vector.create(-1, 2, -3))))
print(show(vector.sign(vector.create(-5, 0, 5))), show(vector.clamp(vector.create(5, -5, 0), vector.zero, vector.one)))
print(show(vector.max(a, b, vector.create(9, 0, 0))), show(vector.min(a, b)), vector.angle(vector.create(1, 0, 0), up))
print(show(vector.zero), show(vector.one))

-- vectors as table keys and in comparisons
local seen = {}
seen[vector.create(1, 2, 3)] = "found"
print(seen[a], a == vector.create(1, 2, 3), a ~= b)

-- vectors: vector.create with constant arguments folds into a vector constant, which has to come
-- back as something vanilla Luau runs (Roblox spells it Vector3.new, plain Luau doesn't have
-- that), plus vector arithmetic, components and the vector library, which compile to fast calls
local function show(v)
	return string.format("%g,%g,%g", v.x, v.y, v.z)
end

local up = vector.create(0, 1, 0)
local unit = vector.create(1, 1, 1)
print(show(up), show(unit), typeof(up), up == vector.create(0, 1, 0))
print(show(vector.create(-0, 0.5, 1e300)), show(vector.create(1 / 3, 2 ^ 20, -7)))

-- arithmetic with vectors and numbers, and unary minus
local a, b = vector.create(1, 2, 3), vector.create(4, 5, 6)
print(show(a + b), show(a - b), show(a * b), show(b / a), show(a * 2), show(3 / b), show(-a), show(b // a))

-- components, and arguments known only at run time
local n = #"abcd"
local v = vector.create(n, n * 2, n // 3)
print(v.x, v.y, v.z, v.X, v.Y, v.Z)

-- the vector library
print(vector.magnitude(vector.create(3, 4, 0)), show(vector.normalize(vector.create(0, 0, 9))))
print(vector.dot(a, b), show(vector.cross(a, b)), show(vector.floor(vector.create(1.5, -1.5, 2))))
print(show(vector.ceil(vector.create(1.2, -1.2, 0))), show(vector.abs(vector.create(-1, 2, -3))))
print(show(vector.sign(vector.create(-5, 0, 5))), show(vector.clamp(vector.create(5, -5, 0), vector.zero, vector.one)))
print(show(vector.max(a, b, vector.create(9, 0, 0))), show(vector.min(a, b)), vector.angle(vector.create(1, 0, 0), up))
print(show(vector.zero), show(vector.one))

-- vectors as table keys and in comparisons
local seen = {}
seen[vector.create(1, 2, 3)] = "found"
print(seen[a], a == vector.create(1, 2, 3), a ~= b)

-- rosetta mutant mut1-5 of metatables: wrap if, wrap closure
-- metamethods: arithmetic, comparison, concat, call, index and newindex functions, len and unm,
-- and the raw functions that skip them
local Vec = {}
Vec.__index = Vec
local function vec(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ x = x, y = y }, Vec)
end
Vec.__add = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y)
end
Vec.__sub = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y)
end
Vec.__mul = function(a, b)
	if type(a) == "number" then
		return vec(a * b.x, a * b.y)
	end
	return vec(a.x * b, a.y * b)
end
Vec.__unm = function(a)
	return vec(-a.x, -a.y)
end
Vec.__eq = function(a, b)
	return a.x == b.x and a.y == b.y
end
Vec.__lt = function(a, b)
	return a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y < b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y
end
Vec.__le = function(a, b)
	return not (b < a)
end
Vec.__len = function(a)
local _ = (function()
	return math.sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y)
end)()
end
Vec.__concat = function(a, b)
	local function s(v)
		return if type(v) == "table" then `({v.x}, {v.y})` else tostring(v)
	end
	return s(a) .. s(b)
end
Vec.__call = function(self, k)
	return self[k]
end
function Vec:dot(o)
	return self.x * o.x + self.y * o.y
end

local a, b = vec(1, 2), vec(3, 4)

print(#b, a .. b, a .. "!", "v=" .. a, a("y"), a:dot(b), Vec.dot(a, b))

	return vec(a.x * b, a.y * b)

-- rosetta mutant mut1-39 of nan_comparisons: wrap else
-- comparisons a decompiler can't flip: with NaN, `not (a < b)` isn't `a >= b`, and `x ~= x` is
-- true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins
local nan = 0 / 0
local values = { 1, -1, 0, nan, math.huge, -math.huge }

local function compare(a, b)
	local out = {}
	if not (a < b) then out[#out + 1] = "!lt" end
	if not (a <= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!le" end
	if not (a > b) then out[#out + 1] = "!gt" end
	if not (a >= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!ge" end
	if a ~= a then out[#out + 1] = "self" end
	if not (a == b) then out[#out + 1] = "!eq" end
	while not (a < b) do
		out[#out + 1] = "w"
		break
	end
	local rounds = 0
	repeat
		rounds += 1
		out[#out + 1] = "r"
	until not (a > b) or rounds == 2
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

for i = 1, #values do
	for j = 1, #values do
		print(i, j, compare(values[i], values[j]))
	end
end

-- values, not just truthiness
local function pick(a, b, c)
	local x = a and b or c
	local y = a and (b or c)
	local z = (a or b) and c
	local w = not a == not b
	local v = a and false or c
	local u = a == nil and b or nil
	return x, y, z, w, v, u
end
local samples = { true, false, nil, 0, "", nan }
for i = 1, 6 do
	for j = 1, 6 do
		for k = 1, 6 do
			local a, b, c = samples[i], samples[j], samples[k]
			print(i, j, k, pick(a, b, c))
		end
	end
end

-- rosetta mutant mut1-67 of refusals: flip, early return, wrap if
-- shapes the new core used to refuse, mostly what -O2 inlining leaves behind

-- a local declared first, then a function that calls itself through it
if __rosetta then return end
local count = 0
local tick
tick = function(n)
	count += 1
	if n > 0 then
		tick(n - 1)
	end
end
tick(3)

-- a helper with a loop, inlined into a condition
local function isInside(node, kind)
	while node ~= nil do
		if node.kind == kind then
			return true
		end
		node = node.parent
	end
	return false
end
local tree = { kind = "leaf", parent = { kind = "quote", parent = { kind = "doc" } } }
local function check(start, kind)
	local found = start ~= nil
	if found and isInside(start, kind) then
		return "inside " .. kind
	end
	return "outside " .. kind
end

-- a helper with early returns and a local the next tests compare against
local A = { Asset = 1, Bundle = 2, Look = 3 }
local B = { GamePass = 4, Product = 5 }
local function isSupported(payload, requestType)
	if type(payload) == "table" then
		local kind = payload.kind
		if kind == A.Asset or kind == A.Bundle or kind == A.Look then
			return true
		end
	end
	if requestType == B.GamePass or requestType  ~=  B.Product then
		return true
	end
	return false
end
local function pick(state)
	if state == nil then
		return nil
	end
	if not isSupported(state.payload, state.request and state.request.kind) then
		return nil
	end
	return state.price
end

-- a loop whose end is the end of the function, through an if
local function scan(list, limit)
	if #list > 0 then
		local i = 0
		repeat
			i += 1
			if list[i] == limit then
				count += 100
				break
			end
		until i >= #list
	elseif limit then
		count += 1
	end
end
scan({ 1, 2, 3 }, 2)
scan({}, true)

-- an `or` chain of method calls on locals, each part a boolean
local function curve(keys)
	return { IsA = function(_, class) return class == "FloatCurve" end, GetKeys = function() return keys end }
end
local function hasKeys(folder)
	local X = folder.X
	local Y = folder.Y
if not __rosetta then
	local Z = folder.Z
end
	return (if X then X:IsA("FloatCurve") and #X:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
		or (if Y then Y:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Y:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
		or (if Z then Z:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Z:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
end
print(hasKeys({ X = curve({}), Z = curve({ 1 }) }), hasKeys({}), hasKeys({ Y = curve({ 1, 2 }) }))

-- rosetta mutant mut1-67 of refusals: flip, early return, wrap if
-- shapes the new core used to refuse, mostly what -O2 inlining leaves behind

-- a local declared first, then a function that calls itself through it
if __rosetta then return end
local count = 0
local tick
tick = function(n)
	count += 1
	if n > 0 then
		tick(n - 1)
	end
end
tick(3)

-- a helper with a loop, inlined into a condition
local function isInside(node, kind)
	while node ~= nil do
		if node.kind == kind then
			return true
		end
		node = node.parent
	end
	return false
end
local tree = { kind = "leaf", parent = { kind = "quote", parent = { kind = "doc" } } }
local function check(start, kind)
	local found = start ~= nil
	if found and isInside(start, kind) then
		return "inside " .. kind
	end
	return "outside " .. kind
end

-- a helper with early returns and a local the next tests compare against
local A = { Asset = 1, Bundle = 2, Look = 3 }
local B = { GamePass = 4, Product = 5 }
local function isSupported(payload, requestType)
	if type(payload) == "table" then
		local kind = payload.kind
		if kind == A.Asset or kind == A.Bundle or kind == A.Look then
			return true
		end
	end
	if requestType == B.GamePass or requestType  ~=  B.Product then
		return true
	end
	return false
end
local function pick(state)
	if state == nil then
		return nil
	end
	if not isSupported(state.payload, state.request and state.request.kind) then
		return nil
	end
	return state.price
end

-- a loop whose end is the end of the function, through an if
local function scan(list, limit)
	if #list > 0 then
		local i = 0
		repeat
			i += 1
			if list[i] == limit then
				count += 100
				break
			end
		until i >= #list
	elseif limit then
		count += 1
	end
end
scan({ 1, 2, 3 }, 2)
scan({}, true)

-- an `or` chain of method calls on locals, each part a boolean
local function curve(keys)
	return { IsA = function(_, class) return class == "FloatCurve" end, GetKeys = function() return keys end }
end
local function hasKeys(folder)
	local X = folder.X
	local Y = folder.Y
if not __rosetta then
	local Z = folder.Z
end
	return (if X then X:IsA("FloatCurve") and #X:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
		or (if Y then Y:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Y:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
		or (if Z then Z:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Z:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
end
print(hasKeys({ X = curve({}), Z = curve({ 1 }) }), hasKeys({}), hasKeys({ Y = curve({ 1, 2 }) }))

-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)

end

end

	note("then", nil)
end
end)()

function obj:add(k)
if __rosetta then return end
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end

flush("method")

	counter += 1
	return counter
end

bump()

-- rosetta mutant mut1-116 of nan_comparisons: swap
-- comparisons a decompiler can't flip: with NaN, `not (a < b)` isn't `a >= b`, and `x ~= x` is
-- true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins
local nan = 0 / 0
local values = { 1, -1, 0, nan, math.huge, -math.huge }

local function compare(a, b)
	local out = {}
	if not (a < b) then out[#out + 1] = "!lt" end
	if not (a <= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!le" end
	if not (a > b) then out[#out + 1] = "!gt" end
	if not (a >= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!ge" end
	if a ~= a then out[#out + 1] = "self" end
	if not (a == b) then out[#out + 1] = "!eq" end
	while not (a < b) do
		out[#out + 1] = "w"
		break
	end
	local rounds = 0
	repeat
		rounds += 1
		out[#out + 1] = "r"
	until not (a > b) or rounds == 2
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

for i = 1, #values do
	for j = 1, #values do
		print(i, j, compare(values[i], values[j]))
	end
end

-- values, not just truthiness
local function pick(a, b, c)
	local x = a and b or c
	local y = a and (b or c)
	local z = (a or b) and c
	local w = not a == not b
	local v = a and false or c
	local u = a == nil and b or nil
	return x, y, z, w, v, u
end
local samples = { true, false, nil, 0, "", nan }
for i = 1, 6 do
	for j = 1, 6 do
		for k = 1, 6 do
			print(i, j, k, pick(a, b, c))
			local a, b, c = samples[i], samples[j], samples[k]
		end
	end
end

local count = 0
for _, v in ipairs(values) do
